title: Finding Three-Branch Piecewise Formulas from Graphs
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find a three-piece formula for each graphed function: (a) a segment from (-1, 1) (closed) to (0, 0) (open), a horizontal segment from (0, 1) (open) to (1, 1) (closed), and a segment from (1, 1) to (3, 0) (open); (b) a segment from (-2, -1) (closed) to (0, 0) (closed), a segment from (0, 2) (open) to (1, 0) (closed), and a horizontal segment from (1, -1) (open) to (3, -1) (closed).
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } f(x) = \begin{cases} -x, & -1 \le x < 0 \\ 1, & 0 < x \le 1 \\ -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{3}{2}, & 1 < x < 3 \end{cases}; \quad \text{(b) } f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{2}x, & -2 \le x \le 0 \\ -2x + 2, & 0 < x \le 1 \\ -1, & 1 < x \le 3 \end{cases}

steps.title: Find the Three Branches of Graph (a)
steps.explanation: In graph (a), note that x = 0 has open circles at both (0, 0) and (0, 1), so 0 is not in the domain. On [-1, 0), the line through (-1, 1) and (0, 0) is y = -x. On (0, 1], the horizontal line is y = 1. On (1, 3), the line through (1, 1) and (3, 0) has slope -1/2, giving y = -x/2 + 3/2.
steps.why: Open circles at (0, 0), (0, 1), and (3, 0) mean x = 0 and x = 3 are excluded from the domain of (a).

steps.title: Find the Three Branches of Graph (b)
steps.mathExpression: y_1 = \frac{1}{2}x \text{ on } [-2, 0]; \quad y_2 = -2x + 2 \text{ on } (0, 1]; \quad y_3 = -1 \text{ on } (1, 3]
steps.explanation: In graph (b), on [-2, 0] the line through (-2, -1) and (0, 0) has slope 1/2, giving y = x/2. On (0, 1], the line from (0, 2) (open) to (1, 0) (closed) has slope -2 and y-intercept 2, giving y = -2x + 2. On (1, 3], the horizontal segment is y = -1.
steps.why: Each transition point x = 0 and x = 1 has one closed dot and one open circle, ensuring a well-defined function on [-2, 3].

steps.title: Write the Complete Piecewise Definitions
steps.mathExpression: \text{(a) } f(x) = \begin{cases} -x, & -1 \le x < 0 \\ 1, & 0 < x \le 1 \\ -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{3}{2}, & 1 < x < 3 \end{cases}, \qquad \text{(b) } f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{2}x, & -2 \le x \le 0 \\ -2x + 2, & 0 < x \le 1 \\ -1, & 1 < x \le 3 \end{cases}
steps.explanation: Assemble the three branches for each graph over their respective subintervals.
steps.why: The piecewise representation captures both the algebraic rule on each segment and the exact endpoint inclusions.
